title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
what_it_shows: 64 legal entities. Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. owns CSC Insurance Group (CSC Property and Casualty Insurance Company and CSC Workers' Compensation Insurance Company, both Florida-domiciled stock insurers with their own boards) and CSC Health Services (340 urgent care and occupational medicine clinics). Corporate shared services staff are employed by the holding company. The register lists no bank, savings association, credit union, broker-dealer, investment adviser or investment company. Organization charts show the Group CISO reporting to the Group CIO with direct access to the board risk committee, the Chief Audit Executive reporting to the audit committee, the division security and compliance leads, and the HIPAA officers of Health Care Services

title: Group: HR roster by division
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: holding company about 5,500, Insurance about 20,500, Health Care Services about 19,000. About 60,000 former employee records. Treasury operations has 24 staff and the plan administration unit in Group HR has 14. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger (SYS-G4); FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Insurance about $14.2 billion (premiums and investment income) and Health Care Services about $3.8 billion. Management fees paid to the holding company eliminate on consolidation

title: Group: 2025 Form 10-K and auditor's report
what_it_shows: The group files as a large accelerated filer. Item 1C describes the group program and its place in enterprise risk management, group internal audit and outside assessors (penetration test, forensic retainer), vendor tiering and SOC report reviews, board risk committee oversight with quarterly Group CISO reports, and the Group CISO and Group Chief Risk Officer roles. The narrative does not mention intercompany services or unmapped complementary controls in vendor reports. The auditor's 2025 attestation on internal control over financial reporting is unqualified

title: Group: disclosure committee charter and minutes
what_it_shows: The charter covers cybersecurity incidents and requires escalation of Severity 1 incidents within 24 hours. Minutes show a yearly review of High cyber risks before filing and no incident determined material in 2025 or 2026 to date. No minutes record a materiality decision using facts from all three divisions, and no method for estimating affected people per division is attached

title: Group: board risk committee and audit committee minutes, 2025 to 2026-03
what_it_shows: The board risk committee approved the group information security program in 2025, reviews strategy outcomes and receives a Group CISO report each quarter; the CEO and the committee own cyber risk. Audit committee minutes of 2026-02 record the 2025 SOX finding on ERP privileged access. The 2026 security budget is approved

title: Group: information security program plan and 2026 strategic plan
what_it_shows: The program plan is aligned to CSF 2.0, approved by the board risk committee in 2025, and ties its priorities to the 2026 strategic plan (a diversified holding company of regulated businesses). Its stakeholder list names the SEC and investors, the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation and commissioners in 5 other states, HHS, independent agencies and employer clients. The metrics pack covers the SOC and identity; it has no division-level measures

title: Group: 2025 group policies, standards and division supplements
what_it_shows: 2025 group policies aligned to CSF 2.0, reviewed each year, with standards for logging (1 year online and 7 years archived for SCSP financial systems), change management, the SCSP configuration management plan, privileged identity, maintenance, procurement and acquisition, design, continuity, authorization and tailoring. SCSP access procedures v2026 sit in the same library. The library has no AI standard. Insurance supplement v2025 was aligned 2025-10; Health Care Services supplement v2023 was aligned 2023-05

title: Group: risk management records
what_it_shows: Risk policy; 2025 risk appetite statement with one cyber limit (no High cyber risk untreated for more than two quarters); the 2025 group enterprise risk register and quarterly risk reports to the board risk committee; monthly risk forum minutes with division security leads; the exception register; and the acceptance matrix: Low by the division security and compliance lead (group risks: the Group CISO's security governance director), Moderate by the division president (group risks: the Group CIO), High by the Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO reported to the board risk committee, Very High by the board risk committee only. No division tolerance is set for payment fraud or PHI exposure

title: Group: 2026 enterprise risk report and insurer registration filings (Fla. Stat. 628.801)
source_system: Group Chief Risk Officer's regulatory filings
what_it_shows: The holding company filed the 2026 enterprise risk report with the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation as ultimate controlling person (628.801(2)), and each insurer filed its annual registration (628.801(1)). The report was drafted from finance risks and describes cyber risk from shared services in general terms. The report is confidential under Fla. Stat. 624.4212

title: Group: internal audit charter and 2026 audit plan
what_it_shows: Group internal audit reports to the audit committee and neither designs nor operates controls. The 2026 plan assesses common controls once and samples division controls, and covers SOX IT general controls with the external auditor

title: Group: 2025 SOX IT general controls workpapers and memo to the audit committee
what_it_shows: 2025 testing of the ERP, HCM and treasury: change advisory board, testing evidence and restricted promotion with no exceptions; interface completeness checks and backups tested; 17 standing ERP superuser accounts, 3 of them for the ERP vendor's support, and ERP emergency access sessions with no review after use. The memo reported the access finding to the audit committee in 2026-02; it was not classified as material

title: Group: identity platform user and authentication export
what_it_shows: About 52,000 workforce identities (employees and contractors), 1,240 service accounts and about 900 federated applications. Number-matching MFA for all workforce users; hardware keys for administrators and for treasury, payroll and ERP privileged users; step-up with a hardware key to release a payment or change a bank template. Lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based blocking; passwords of at least 14 characters checked against breached-password lists; SCSP sessions end after 15 minutes idle and 12 hours absolute; tokens bound to the device; conditional access limits treasury release to managed devices on group networks in business hours and blocks unmanaged devices for the ERP, HCM and treasury; bank and administrator vendor users sign in through federation or named guest accounts with MFA; the sign-in page shows the system use notice

title: Group: identity governance and service account reports
what_it_shows: Joiner, mover and leaver workflows run from HCM events; temporary accounts carry end dates; accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled except sealed break-glass accounts; quarterly certification campaigns cover federated applications including the ERP, HCM and treasury. The service account register lists 112 of 1,240 service accounts with no named owner; service accounts are not in the certification campaigns; 41 static service account keys are older than 1 year. Median time from HCM termination to account disablement is 38 minutes. A high-risk disablement runbook has a 2026 test record

title: Group: SYS-G1 role assignment and privileged access reports
what_it_shows: 212 accounts hold group-wide identity administration, password reset or MFA reset rights, including 61 division help desk agents. 9 named identity engineers can change SYS-G1 security settings through PAM. Directory and cloud administrator rights are granted just in time through PAM with approval and session recording; administrators use separate privileged identities; privileged commands run only from PAM jump hosts; vendor remote maintenance on directory servers and integration services goes through PAM. The 17 ERP superuser accounts are standing accounts outside PAM

title: Group: help desk reset procedure, reset log and onboarding proofing
source_system: Group service desk knowledge base; SYS-G1 audit log
what_it_shows: The password and MFA reset procedure asks the caller for an employee ID and the manager's name; the lost or compromised authenticator procedure has the same check. The 90-day reset log records each reset with the agent, the division help desk and the user. Workforce identities are proofed by HR at hire. The help desk curriculum has no module on social engineering of resets

title: Group: corporate directory and trust report
what_it_shows: 6 corporate directory servers in the colocation data center and provider A, upgraded in 2025 and patched within 14 days for critical issues. A two-way trust links the corporate forest with the local directory of the 50 clinics acquired in 2025. The interconnection register has no entry, agreement or risk acceptance for the trust

title: Group: interconnection register and integration route catalog
source_system: SCSP integration services console; GRC tool
what_it_shows: Approved routes connect division systems, the four SCSP applications and 14 banks; bank and plan administrator exchanges have agreements with interface details and impact levels; functions, ports and protocols are documented; the catalog is reviewed each quarter. Payment and payroll files are validated against approved templates and totals, and hash and record counts are checked between the integration services and the banks. A scheduled benefits export from SYS-G5 to a general HR collaboration site in SYS-G7 was added in 2025. Claims disbursement file exchanges with SYS-I2 and SYS-I4 refer to the 2017 intercompany agreement and list no security requirements

title: Group: SIEM data sources, detection and retention configuration
what_it_shows: Data sources include SYS-G1, the SCSP applications, endpoints, email, hub flow logs and division applications; the legacy directory and the legacy EHR at the 50 acquired clinics are not in the list. Behavior analytics cover workforce accounts and exclude service account sign-ins and help desk MFA resets. Correlation rules span divisions; alerts fire on privileged role assignment outside a ticket, payment template changes and mass HCM exports; automated containment revokes sessions and disables accounts. Logs are kept 1 year online and 7 years archived with write-once retention; 6 SOC engineers can manage retention settings; a data source health dashboard is kept

title: Group: SOC case records, playbooks and weekly reports, 2025 to 2026-03
what_it_shows: 24x7 triage and case management; weekly reports to each system owner, including the SCSP platform director; playbooks for identity compromise, payment fraud and ransomware with impact estimation and recovery criteria; alerts routed to division liaisons; investigations with an Insurance liaison; forensic analysis with the retainer firm and chain of custody; case records kept 7 years; Severity 1 declaration criteria in the group severity scale

title: Group: EDR and email security console reports
what_it_shows: EDR runs on endpoints, servers, directory servers, jump hosts, integration compute, virtual machines and container hosts, and clinic workstations; application control on servers; users cannot install software on managed endpoints without approval; email security covers all mailboxes

title: Group: vulnerability scan reports and 2026 penetration test report
source_system: Vulnerability scanner console; penetration test report
what_it_shows: Weekly authenticated scans of integration services and directory servers with daily signature updates; critical findings closed within 14 days. The external penetration test of the SCSP integration services and identity platform in 2026-03 reported no critical issues

title: Group: incident response plan, exercise reports and notification matrix
what_it_shows: The group incident response plan is approved by the board risk committee, with an Insurance annex and a distribution list. Exercise reports for 2025 and 2026 to date record quarterly technical playbook tests and no exercise across divisions. The notification matrix has rows for the SEC, HIPAA for Health Care Services and state breach laws; it has no rows for insurance commissioners in states that enacted Model #668, notices to producers of record, or the group health plan. The plan's vendor contacts do not include the health plan administrator or the legacy EHR hosting provider. Contact lists name law enforcement and the cyber insurer, not the insurers' state regulators. The communications plan has no holding statements for policyholders and agencies

title: Group: cyber insurance program and forensic retainer
what_it_shows: A group cyber insurance program with a breach response panel; a forensic retainer firm engaged through the panel

title: Group: threat intelligence subscriptions and advisory log
source_system: SOC threat intelligence platform; public website
what_it_shows: Threat intelligence from sector sharing communities, integrated in the SIEM; advisories reviewed daily and shared with reinsurers through a secure channel; a vulnerability disclosure intake page on the public sites

title: Group: cloud account inventory, IAM export and CMDB reconciliation
source_system: Cloud provider consoles (providers A and B); CMDB
what_it_shows: Provider A hosts the landing zone hub, the SCSP integration services and managed file transfer, SYS-I1, SYS-I2, SYS-I3, SYS-H2 and SYS-H3. Provider B hosts the immutable backup vault and warm standbys for the SCSP integration services and SYS-I2. The colocation data center hosts SYS-I4 and corporate directory servers. Each division has its own accounts with roles federated from SYS-G1. Capacity dashboards cover the integration services and the claims platform, with catastrophe scaling for claims. The CMDB is reconciled monthly against cloud and SaaS records; its software and service entries for the 50 acquired clinics are incomplete

title: Group: landing-zone guardrail compliance report
what_it_shows: Guardrails (encryption, logging, no public storage, approved services and regions) apply to every division account; deviations carry approved exceptions; unused services and ports are disabled on integration services

title: Group: network diagram and hub firewall rule base
what_it_shows: The hub denies traffic by default between division accounts and the SCSP. Integration services sit in private subnets with no VPN path; bank connections use private links or mutual TLS; encrypted private links reach the colocation data center and clinic WAN tunnels; cellular failover at every clinic. Provider DDoS protection and web application firewall rules front the public portals. The 50 acquired clinics run flat networks behind the legacy directory trust

title: Group: key management configuration
source_system: Key management services (providers A and B)
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys per account with rotation for integration storage, backups and the employer portal database; FIPS-validated cryptography where the services offer it

title: Group: backup vault configuration and backup and restore reports
what_it_shows: Immutable backups of cloud workloads in provider B with a backup identity separate from production; colocation backups, including SYS-I4, copied nightly to the same vault; integration services and configuration backed up daily; ERP, HCM and treasury data exported nightly; restore tests each quarter; the SYS-I4 restore is tested once a year

title: Group: continuity plans and 2026 recovery test records
what_it_shows: The integration services failover test on 2026-02-21 took 6 hours against a 4-hour RTO, and no retest is scheduled. Identity and network recovery tests in 2026 met their 1-hour and 2-hour RTOs; treasury recovery was tested in 2026. The SCSP contingency plan v2026, recovery runbooks (identity first, then integration, then treasury and payroll) and the reconciliation procedure to bank confirmations are on file; tests are coordinated with banks and the payroll provider; sealed break-glass accounts are tested quarterly; contingency roles are trained each year

title: Group: TLS scan of external and integration endpoints
what_it_shows: All scanned endpoints, including remote access, portals and bank connections, accept TLS 1.2 or higher with approved ciphers

title: Group: provider assurance reports, colocation access list and badge access reviews
source_system: Provider compliance portals; colocation provider portal
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports from providers A and B and the colocation provider cover physical access, environmental controls and media sanitization; the colocation cage access list is reviewed each quarter; wipe certificates are kept for group endpoints before reuse; badge access lists for group and Insurance offices are reviewed each quarter

title: Group: ERP role catalog, segregation-of-duties ruleset and superuser list
what_it_shows: 3,100 users across 64 entities with roles by entity and function; the ruleset separates vendor master changes, invoice entry and payment proposal; 17 standing superuser accounts, 3 of them for the ERP vendor's support; the emergency access log; quarterly certification of ERP roles; the invoice capture feature is in use in payables

title: Group: HCM role catalog, benefits export and HR site permissions
source_system: HCM admin console (SYS-G5); productivity suite admin console (SYS-G7)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employee and about 60,000 former employee records; roles by population; payroll administrators hold broad HCM reporting rights. A scheduled benefits export lands on a general HR collaboration site that about 140 HR staff outside the plan administration unit can open; plan administration files (appeals and stop-loss claims) sit on the same site. HCM sends the eligibility feed to the health plan's third-party administrator

title: Group: treasury users, release log and payment volumes
what_it_shows: 260 users at 14 banks. About $65 million in outgoing payments per business day (claims disbursements, payroll funding and payables): about 1,900 wires and 140,000 ACH entries. Dual approval and positive pay on releases; one concurrent session per user; the release log records the authenticated session, the bank confirmation, the device and prior and new beneficiary values; a callback standard applies to urgent payment requests

title: Group: data processing, purpose and data sharing registers
what_it_shows: Authority and purpose recorded per data category for HCM, payroll and benefits data, including the plan sponsor's limited authority for plan administration PHI; sharing with payroll banks, the plan administrator and auditors needs an approval naming purpose and recipient. Data inventories exist for HCM and the EHR. No register records where PHI, consumer nonpublic information or MNPI sit in collaboration sites

title: Group: change records, pipeline and repository settings
what_it_shows: Change advisory board approvals with testing evidence for SCSP, portal and fraud model releases; emergency changes reviewed within 2 business days; the standard change template includes a security impact analysis; only release engineers can promote changes; protected branches; static analysis and integration tests before release; software integrity checks in the pipeline; baseline configurations kept as code or exported monthly

title: Group: vendor SOC 2 report reviews for the SCSP SaaS vendors
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports from the identity, ERP, HCM and treasury vendors are reviewed each year; the ERP vendor review does not map the report's complementary user entity controls to owners; ERP vendor support works through the 3 standing superuser accounts, and its activity is not in the PAM session records

title: Group: productivity suite sharing, labeling and device report
source_system: Productivity suite admin console (SYS-G7); device management
what_it_shows: No sensitivity labels are configured for PHI, consumer nonpublic information or MNPI. Deal-room exports have been copied to general collaboration sites, and plan administration files sit on the general HR site. Managed endpoints lock after 10 minutes and block unapproved software

title: Group: board portal and virtual data room configuration
source_system: Board portal and data room admin consoles (SYS-G8)
what_it_shows: Board portal access requires MFA and documents are watermarked; virtual data rooms allow users to export documents

title: Group: training completion and phishing simulation reports
what_it_shows: 98% completion of the 2025 annual security training, which includes insider threat awareness and reporting channels; quarterly phishing simulations; role training for treasury, payroll and ERP administrators on payment fraud and change control; annual incident response training for the SOC, SCSP staff and division liaisons; annual HIPAA training for the plan administration unit and Health Care Services. No module covers social engineering of help desk resets or payment-change fraud in the call center

title: Group: screening, acknowledgment and sanctions records
what_it_shows: Background checks for all hires and enhanced checks for treasury and payroll staff; confidentiality and acceptable use agreements signed at hire and acknowledged each year; contractor security terms with a named sponsor; the sanctions log; transfers trigger role recertification within 5 business days

title: Group: vendor master, tiering and contract register
source_system: Accounts payable vendor master (SYS-G4); third-party risk tool; contract management system
what_it_shows: Suppliers across divisions tiered by criticality; tier 1 vendors reviewed each year with SOC 2 reports; vendor templates carry security, breach notice within 72 hours, audit and exit terms; data return not verified for 2 retired vendors. Contract recovery point objectives are 1 hour for the ERP, HCM and treasury SaaS and 15 minutes for the clinic EHR vendor. The vendor risk standard and supply chain plan cover outside suppliers; intercompany services are not in the vendor inventory

title: Group: intercompany services agreements and business associate agreement
what_it_shows: The 2017 intercompany services agreement covers claims payment processing and identity services from the holding company to the insurers and has no security requirements, service levels or incident notice terms. The 2019 services agreement covers shared services to Health Care Services; the 2021 business associate agreement requires breach notice within 10 days and includes the required terms, including incident reporting. Neither document mentions the AI assistant or the patient refund file flow through treasury

title: Group: AI tool discovery
source_system: Procurement and SaaS discovery; SYS-G1 application list; Insurance model registry
what_it_shows: AI in use or proposed: a generative AI add-on to SYS-G7 licensed for a 6,000-user pilot planned to start 2026-05-04; the in-house claims triage and fraud scoring model on SYS-I2; the photo-estimating vendor's model; a proposed homeowners pricing model using aerial imagery attributes; the bill review vendor's machine learning rules; the EHR vendor's urgent care triage and sepsis alert; a proposal for an AI scribe pilot at 12 clinics; resume screening in the HCM recruiting module, switched on by the vendor in 2026-03; ERP invoice capture; and a coding assistant for SCSP integration code. The policy library has no AI standard

title: Group: records retention schedules
what_it_shows: Group retention schedule for HCM, payroll, ERP and treasury records; the insurers' 2019 retention schedule for claim files; no automated purge of closed claims is configured in SYS-I2 or SYS-I4

title: Group health plan: plan documents, sponsor certification and administrator BAA
what_it_shows: Plan documents were amended in 2014 to restrict the sponsor's use of PHI (164.504(f)) and name the 14-person plan administration unit; the plan was restated in 2019; the sponsor certification was signed in 2014 and not re-signed; the plan documents contain no 164.314(b)(2) security terms. The third-party administrator's BAA dates from 2022

title: Group health plan: enrollment and claims summary
what_it_shows: Self-insured medical plan for employees of all three divisions: about 38,000 participants and 92,000 covered lives. Claims are processed by the third-party administrator; 2025 claims show about 9,000 covered lives treated at the group's clinics. The administrator's SOC 2 report is reviewed each year

title: Group health plan: privacy and security official designations
what_it_shows: The Group benefits director is the plan's privacy official. The Group security governance director was designated the plan's security official by letter dated 2026-02-02

title: Insurance: licenses, domicile and agency channel
what_it_shows: Both insurers are Florida-domiciled stock insurers licensed in Florida, Georgia, Alabama, South Carolina, North Carolina and Tennessee; neither holds a New York license. Sales run through about 2,400 independent agencies and a direct channel

title: Insurance: state law tracker for Model #668 and the NAIC AI Model Bulletin
what_it_shows: Among the 6 licensed states, the tracker lists Alabama and South Carolina as having enacted Model #668 and Tennessee for portions of it; Florida, Georgia and North Carolina have general breach and privacy statutes only. North Carolina adopted the NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of AI Systems by Insurers (Bulletin No. 24-B-19, 2024-12-18) per the NAIC map as of 2026-04-01; no other licensed state has. State text varies; insurance counsel confirms each enacted version

title: Insurance: written information security programs and 2025 board reports
what_it_shows: Programs for both insurers adopted 2019 and updated 2025, building on the group program; board resolutions designate the Insurance information security officer; written reports delivered to each insurer board in 2025 do not cover the holding company's services; the 2025 Insurance inheritance matrix lists the group common controls; the program change log ends in 2025; common controls are run by the Group CISO with no written delegate report to insurer management

title: Insurance: policy, consumer and claims volumes
what_it_shows: About 3.1 million policies in force: 1.9 million personal auto, 1.0 million homeowners and 160,000 workers' compensation. Nonpublic information on about 6.8 million consumers (policyholders, insureds, claimants and applicants). About 1.2 million claims a year

title: Insurance: call center bank-detail change procedure and claims authority matrix
what_it_shows: Claimant and repair shop bank-detail changes for claims disbursements can be made through the call center after knowledge-based questions; the procedure has no callback to contact data on file. Adjusters may approve claim payments up to $25,000 without a second approval; payment limits and treasury positive pay review apply

title: Insurance: catastrophe surge onboarding procedure and 2025 surge records
source_system: Catastrophe team records; SYS-G1 identity governance
what_it_shows: The procedure targets up to 1,500 independent adjuster accounts within 72 hours of a hurricane declaration; identities come from adjusting-firm rosters and are checked with knowledge questions; accounts are pre-staged disabled, expire automatically and are limited to assigned claims. 1,180 surge adjusters were onboarded for the 2025 hurricane season

title: Insurance: SYS-I4 contingency plan, recovery estimate and server inventory
what_it_shows: The workers' compensation platform runs only in the colocation data center, with nightly backups to disk and the provider B vault; rebuild from the vault is estimated at 36 hours; two application servers run an operating system past vendor support and sit on an isolated network segment with EDR

title: Insurance: claims platform roles, logging and disposal records
source_system: SYS-I2 admin console; Insurance records management
what_it_shows: Claim access by line and region; payment-change screens limited to the claims payment unit; claim, reserve, payment and bank-detail change events logged and sent to the SIEM; laptops encrypted; media sanitization records on file

title: Insurance: customer and agent identity configuration
what_it_shows: MFA required for agents and optional for policyholders; bot detection and lockout; export limits on quotes and policy lookups; agency user offboarding depends on notice from the agency; web application firewall rules on the portals

title: Insurance: vendor files and reinsurance contract register
source_system: Insurance vendor management; reinsurance contract register
what_it_shows: The estimating and bill review vendors have security terms and annual SOC 2 reviews that cover security, not model governance; the photo-estimating vendor keeps claim photos 7 years. The insurers cede risk to reinsurers and assume none. Ad hoc reinsurance and audit data requests are sent by email with opportunistic TLS. There is no vendor file for the holding company

title: Insurance: claims fraud scoring model documentation and monitoring

title: Insurance: workers' compensation claims and clinic network report

About 6.1 million visits and 2.4 million unique patients a year; about 6,200 employer clients for occupational health. title: Health Care Services: EHR role configuration and privacy monitoring reports
